newsitem.title: UK: IRA operations incompatible with peace -Britain.
newsitem.headline: IRA operations incompatible with peace -Britain.

text.p: Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary said on Thursday that recent attempted outrages by the Irish Republican Army were incompatible with its leaders' claim that they want peace in the province.

"It is of great interest to the people of Northern Ireland to conjecture how this sort of behaviour is compatible with the language of peace and the language of democracy which at the same time the IRA and those who speak for them espouse," Sir Patrick Mayhew told parliament.

On Wednesday night, police found a primed M16 mortar in alleyway near to a British army base in Northern Ireland, a few hours after receiving a telephone call warning, which Mayhew said used an IRA codeword, of a bomb in the area.
Mayhew had been asked by Ulster Unionist leader David Trimble whether "these actions are a more reliable guide to the intentions of Sinn Fein/IRA than the rumours of a ceasefire".
He replied: "I regretfully have to endorse what you have said."
Britain and Ireland are refusing to allow Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, to enter all-party talks on the future of Northern Ireland until the IRA declares a credible ceasefire.
"It is abundantly clear that there is a great gap between the conduct of the IRA ...and what is necessary to allow Sinn Fein to enter the talks," Mayhew said.
"They have to show that they are firmly committed to peace and they have to show that they are firmly committed to the democratic process." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
